arxiv-2108-13065.title: Proposed Negative Thermal Expansion in Honeycomb-Lattice Antiferromagnets
arxiv-2108-13065.creator: Yuto Uwabo, Masahito Mochizuki
arxiv-2108-13065.description: Abstract We theoretically propose possible magnetism-induced negative thermal expansion in honeycomb-lattice antiferromagnets with edge-sharing networks of M ​ X 6 MX_{6} octahedra where M M and X X are transition-metal and ligand ions, respectively. In this crystal structure, the nearest-neighbor exchange interaction is composed of two competing contributions, i.e.

arxiv-2201-04632.title: The Concept of Action Criticality in AI Safety
arxiv-2201-04632.creator: Yitzhak Spielberg
arxiv-2201-04632.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yitzhak Spielberg. When AI agents don’t align their actions with human values they may cause serious harm. One way to solve the value alignment problem is by including a human operator who monitors all of the agent’s actions. Despite the fact, that this solution guarantees maximal safety, it is very inefficient, since it requires the human operator to dedicate all of his attention to the agent.

arxiv-2208-06572.title: Demo: RhythmEdge: Enabling Contactless Heart Rate Estimation on the Edge
arxiv-2208-06572.creator: Zahid Hasan † , Emon Dey † , Sreenivasan Ramasamy Ramamurthy † , Nirmalya Roy † , Archan Misra §
arxiv-2208-06572.description: Abstract In this demo paper, we design and prototype RhythmEdge [ 1 ] , a low-cost, deep-learning-based contact-less system for regular HR monitoring applications. RhythmEdge benefits over existing approaches by facilitating contact-less nature, real-time/offline operation, inexpensive and available sensing components, and computing devices.

arxiv-2305-00927.title: Cross-Institutional Transfer Learning for Educational Models: Implications for Model Performance, Fairness, and Equity Conference: 2023 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency; June 12–15, 2023; Chicago, IL, USA 2023 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (
arxiv-2305-00927.creator: Josh Gardner, Renzhe Yu, Quan Nguyen, Christopher Brooks, Rene F. Kizilcec
arxiv-2305-00927.description: Abstract . Modern machine learning increasingly supports paradigms that are multi-institutional (using data from multiple institutions during training) or cross-institutional (using models from multiple institutions for inference), but the empirical effects of these paradigms are not well understood. This study investigates cross-institutional learning via an empirical case study in higher education.

arxiv-2310-13789.creator: Rémi Cocou Avohou, Reiko Toriumi, Matthias Vancraeynest
arxiv-2310-13789.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Rémi Cocou Avohou, Reiko Toriumi, Matthias Vancraeynest. The authors studied in [Ann. Henri Poincaré D 9, 367-433, (2022)], a complex multi-matrix model with U ​ ( N ) 2 × O ⁡ ( D ) \mathrm{U}(N)^{2}\times\mathrm{O}(D) symmetry, and whose double scaling limit where simultaneously the large- N N and large- D D limits were taken while keeping the ratio N / D = M N/\sqrt{D}=M finite and fixed.

arxiv-2403-07956.title: DeepCDCL : An CDCL-based Neural Network Verification Framework
arxiv-2403-07956.creator: Zongxin Liu, Pengfei Yang, Lijun Zhang, Xiaowei Huang
arxiv-2403-07956.description: Abstract Neural networks in safety-critical applications face increasing safety and security concerns due to their susceptibility to little disturbance. In this paper, we propose DeepCDCL , a novel neural network verification framework based on the Conflict-Driven Clause Learning (CDCL) algorithm.

arxiv-2403-13045.title: Sites of Planet Formation in Binary Systems. I. Evidence for Disk-Orbit Alignment in the Close Binary FO Tau Facilities: ALMA, Texas Advanced Computing Center (TACC), Keck:II (NIRC2,NIRSPEC) astropy ( Price-Whelan et al. 2018 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ) , emcee ( Foreman-Mackey et al. 2013
arxiv-2403-13045.creator: Benjamin M. Tofflemire, Lisa Prato, Adam L. Kraus, Dominique Segura-Cox, G. H. Schaefer, Rachel Akeson, Sean Andrews, Eric L. N. Jensen, Christopher M. Johns-Krull, J. J. Zanazzi, M. Simon
arxiv-2403-13045.description: Abstract Close binary systems present challenges to planet formation. As binary separations decrease, so too do the occurrence rates of protoplanetary disks in young systems and planets in mature systems. For systems that do retain disks, their disk masses and sizes are altered by the presence of the binary companion.

arxiv-2502-02674.title: Confidence intervals for functionals in constrained inverse problems via data-adaptive sampling-based calibration
arxiv-2502-02674.creator: Michael Stanley, Pau Batlle, Pratik Patil, Houman Owhadi, Mikael Kuusela
arxiv-2502-02674.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Michael Stanley, Pau Batlle, Pratik Patil, Houman Owhadi, Mikael Kuusela. We address functional uncertainty quantification for ill-posed inverse problems with rank-deficient forward models, known observation noise distributions, and parameter constraints common in scientific applications such as remote sensing and high-energy physics. We propose four constraint-aware confidence interval methods built upon a theoretical test inversion framework in [ 2 ] and optimization-based endpoint computations, resulting in intervals that are both computationally feasible and less conservative.

arxiv-2502-09712.title: The fall of asteroid 2024 XA 1 and the location of possible meteorites
arxiv-2502-09712.creator: Francesco Gianotto, Albino Carbognani, Marco Fenucci, Maxime Devogèle, Pablo Ramirez-Moreta, Marco Micheli, Raffaele Salerno, Toni Santana-Ros, Juan Luis Cano, Luca Conversi, Charlie Drury, Laura Faggioli, Dora Föhring, Reiner Kresken, Selina Machnitzky, Richard Moissl, Francisco Ocaña, Dario Olivie
arxiv-2502-09712.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Francesco Gianotto, Albino Carbognani, Marco Fenucci, Maxime Devogèle, Pablo Ramirez-Moreta, Marco Micheli, Raffaele Salerno, Toni Santana-Ros, Juan Luis Cano, Luca Conversi, Charlie Drury, Laura Faggioli, Dora Föhring, Reiner Kresken, Selina Machnitzky, Richard Moissl, Francisco Ocaña, Dario Olivie. Asteroid 2024 XA 1 was discovered on 3 December 2024 at 05:54 UTC by the Bok telescope in Kitt Peak, Arizona, and impacted Earth about 10 hours later over a remote area of the Sakha Republic (Russia).

arxiv-2507-19183.title: Agentic AI and Hallucinations
arxiv-2507-19183.creator: Engin Iyidogan, Ali I. Ozkes
arxiv-2507-19183.description: Abstract We model a competitive market where AI agents buy answers from upstream generative models and resell them to users who differ in how much they value accuracy and in how much they fear hallucinations. Agents can privately exert effort for costly verification to lower hallucination risks.

arxiv-2509-08734.title: DEQuify your force field: More efficient simulations using deep equilibrium models
arxiv-2509-08734.creator: Andreas Burger, Luca Thiede, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Nandita Vijaykumar
arxiv-2509-08734.description: Abstract Machine learning force fields show great promise in enabling more accurate molecular dynamics simulations compared to manually derived ones. Much of the progress in recent years was driven by exploiting prior knowledge about physical systems, in particular symmetries under rotation, translation, and reflections.

arxiv-2510-19129.title: Dependent Session Types for Verified Concurrent Programming Journal: PACMPL Volume: 1 CONF 1
arxiv-2510-19129.creator: Qiancheng Fu, Hongwei Xi, Ankush Das
arxiv-2510-19129.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Qiancheng Fu, Hongwei Xi, Ankush Das. We present TLL C which extends the Two-Level Linear dependent type theory (TLL) with session-based concurrency. Equipped with Martin-Löf style dependency, the session types of TLL C allow protocols to specify properties of communicated messages. When used in conjunction with the dependent type machinery already present in TLL, dependent session types facilitate a form of relational verification by relating concurrent programs with their idealized sequential counterparts.

arxiv-2511-23240.title: Identifying genuine entanglement of lossy noisy very large scale continuous variable Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger state
arxiv-2511-23240.creator: Xiao-yu Chen
arxiv-2511-23240.description: Abstract Genuine entanglement identification of large scale systems is crucial for quantum computation, quantum communication and quantum learning advantage. In contrast to experiments, where noisy intermediate-scale programmable photonic quantum processors have been developed, theoretically very limited results have been achieved for detecting genuine entanglement of continuous variable multipartite systems.

arxiv-2512-06822.title: Inertial rotation of a small oblate spheroid in a simple shear flow
arxiv-2512-06822.creator: Z. Wang 1, X. M. de Wit 1, D. Di Giusto 2,3, L. Bergougnoux 3, É. Guazzelli 4, C. Marchioli 2, B. Mehlig 5, F. Toschi 1,6
arxiv-2512-06822.description: Abstract We compare experiments and fully-resolved particle simulations designed to match the experimental conditions of a weakly inertial, neutrally buoyant, moderately oblate spheroid in shear flow under confinement. Experimental and numerical results are benchmarked against theory valid for asymptotically small particle Reynolds numbers and for unconfined systems.

arxiv-2602-19725.title: Damped harmonic oscillator revisited: a new approach to energy decay in the case of Coulomb, Stokes, and Newton damping
arxiv-2602-19725.creator: Robert Pezer, Karlo Lelas
arxiv-2602-19725.description: Abstract Approximate formulas are derived to describe energy loss in a harmonic oscillator that experiences three distinct damping mechanisms: constant-magnitude (Coulomb), velocity-proportional (Stokes), and velocity-squared (Newton), using fundamental mathematical methods and physical insight. Our methodology leverages an understanding of the free harmonic oscillator and the inherent link between energy dissipation rates and the power exerted by damping forces.

arxiv-2604-24491.title: Torus one-point functions in critical loop models
arxiv-2604-24491.creator: Paul Roux, Sylvain Ribault, Jesper Lykke Jacobsen

catholic-encyclopedia-1913-veneration-of.title: Veneration of Images (Catholic Encyclopedia article)
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-veneration-of.creator: Adrian Fortescue
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-veneration-of.description: Article 'Veneration of Images' from the Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), the 15-volume English-language reference work published 1907-1914 by Robert Appleton Company.

pmc-10506894.title: Interspecific Variation in the Inner Ear Maculae of Sharks
pmc-10506894.creator: Derek J Sauer, Kara E Yopak, Craig A Radford
pmc-10506894.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). SynopsisThere is well-documented diversity in the organization of inner ear hair cells in fishes; this variation is thought to reflect the differing functional requirements of species across a range of ecological niches. However, relatively little is known about interspecific variation (and its potential ecological implications) in the number and density of inner ear hair cells in elasmobranchs (sharks, skates, and rays).

pmc-10594044.title: Methylation of ESR1 promoter induced by SNAI2–DNMT3B complex promotes epithelial–mesenchymal transition and correlates with poor prognosis in ERα‐positive breast cancers
pmc-10594044.creator: Ji‐Wei Li, Qiu‐Min Deng, Jian‐Ling Zhu, Wei Min, Xiao‐Yi Hu, Hong‐ Yu Chen, Zhong Luo, Lin‐Ling Lin, Xiao‐Long Wei, Yong‐Qu Zhang, Kang‐Liang Lou, Yi‐Yang Gao, Guo‐Jun Zhang, Jing‐Wen Bai
pmc-10594044.description: Estrogen receptor α (ERα) serves as an essential therapeutic predictor for breast cancer (BC) patients and is regulated by epigenetic modification. Abnormal methylation of cytosine phosphoric acid guanine islands in the estrogen receptor 1 (ESR1) gene promoter could silence or decrease ERα expression.

pmc-10611187.title: An Emergency Coordinated Control Strategy to Improve the Transient Stability of a Single-Ended Distribution Network with Flexible Interconnection Channel Blocking
pmc-10611187.creator: Rui Ma, Haichang Sun, Liang Qin
pmc-10611187.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Based on the scenario of high-penetration distributed photovoltaic connected to an AC/DC distribution network, this paper analyzes the dynamic characteristics of frequency and voltage in a distribution network after the blocking failure of the flexible interconnection channel. In order to enhance the transient stability of the system after the fault, this paper comprehensively considers the active regulation ability of photovoltaic units, and puts forward an emergency coordinated control strategy for a single-ended distribution network with flexible interconnection channel blocking.

pmc-10619510.title: Exploring the roles of ZmARM gene family in maize development and abiotic stress response
pmc-10619510.creator: Zhijia Yu, Xiaopeng Sun, Ziqi Chen, Qi Wang, Chuang Zhang, Xiangguo Liu, Weilin Wu, Yuejia Yin
pmc-10619510.description: Armadillo (ARM) was a gene family important to plants, with crucial roles in regulating plant growth, development, and stress responses. However, the properties and functions of ARM family members in maize had received limited attention. Therefore, this study employed bioinformatics methods to analyze the structure and evolution of ARM-repeat protein family members in maize. The maize (Zea mays L.

pmc-10630234.title: Genes positively regulated by Mef2c in cortical neurons are enriched for common genetic variation associated with IQ and educational attainment
pmc-10630234.creator: Laura Fahey, Deema Ali, Gary Donohoe, Pilib Ó Broin, Derek W Morris
pmc-10630234.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The myocyte enhancer factor 2 C (MEF2C) gene encodes a transcription factor important for neurogenesis and synapse development and contains common variants associated with intelligence (IQ) and educational attainment (EA). Here, we took gene expression data from the mouse cortex of a Mef2c mouse model with a heterozygous DNA binding-deficient mutation of Mef2c (Mef2c-het) and combined these data with MEF2C ChIP-seq data from cortical neurons and single-cell data from the mouse brain.

pmc-10631066.title: Duck Tembusu virus induces incomplete autophagy via the ERK/mTOR and AMPK/mTOR signalling pathways to promote viral replication in neuronal cells
pmc-10631066.creator: Qing Wang, Yaqian Jiang, Guangbin Bao, Weiping Yao, Qing Yang, Shuyue Chen, Guijun Wang
pmc-10631066.description: Duck Tembusu virus (DTMUV) is a neurotropic virus in the genus Flavivirus that causes massive economic losses to the poultry industry in China and neighbouring countries. Autophagy is pivotal in cellular responses to pathogens and in viral pathogenesis. However, little is known about the roles of autophagy in DTMUV replication and viral pathogenesis, especially in neuropathogenesis.

pmc-10646675.title: Investigating Attraction and Retention of Staff Within Public Mental Health Services in Victoria, Australia: Protocol for a Mixed Methods Study
pmc-10646675.creator: Kaitlyn Crocker, Inge Gnatt, Darren Haywood, Ravi Bhat, Ingrid Butterfield, Anoop Raveendran Nair Lalitha, Ruby Bishop, David J Castle, Zoe M Jenkins, Amaryllis Mavragani, Ali AL-Asadi, Todd Benham
pmc-10646675.description: BackgroundA large proportion of Australians are affected by mental illness each year, and treatment gaps are well known. To meet current and future demands and enable access to treatment that is safe, effective, and acceptable, a robust and sustainable mental health workforce is required.

pmc-11312966.title: Comprehensive analysis, diagnosis, prognosis, and cordycepin (CD) regulations for GSDME expressions in pan-cancers
pmc-11312966.creator: Jiewen Fu, Dabing Li, Lianmei Zhang, Mazaher Maghsoudloo, Jingliang Cheng, Junjiang Fu
pmc-11312966.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The Gasdermin E gene (GSDME) plays roles in deafness and cancers. However, the roles and mechanisms in cancers are complex, and the same gene exhibits different mechanisms and actions in different types of cancers. Online databases, such as GEPIA2, cBioPortal, and DNMIVD, were used to comprehensively analyze GSDME profiles, DNA methylations, mutations, diagnosis, and prognosis in patients with tumor tissues and matched healthy tissues.

pmc-11336887.title: MZT2A serves as a prognostic biomarker and promotes the progression of kidney renal clear cell carcinoma
pmc-11336887.creator: Li Cao, Xintao Jing, Lijuan Liu, Hui Wang, Jiaqi Zhu, Jing Zhou, Hang Peng, Jinyuan Zhang, Fang Li, Xiaofei Wang, Le Zhao
pmc-11336887.description: MZT2A is a novel core component in the γ-tubulin ring complex and aberrantly expressed in some types of tumors. However, MZT2A expression pattern across different cancers and its role in kidney renal clear cell carcinoma have not been sufficiently investigated.

pmc-11352481.title: Blocking Thromboxane-Prostanoid Receptor Signaling Attenuates Lipopolysaccharide- and Stearic Acid-Induced Inflammatory Response in Human PBMCs
pmc-11352481.creator: Vinothkumar Rajamanickam, Cyrus V Desouza, Romilia T Castillo, Viswanathan Saraswathi, Roger Schneiter
pmc-11352481.description: Inflammation is implicated in the etiology of obesity-related diseases. Thromboxane-prostanoid receptor (TPR) is known to play a role in mediating an inflammatory response in a variety of cells. Gut-derived lipopolysaccharide (LPS), a TLR4 agonist, is elevated in obesity. Moreover, free fatty acids (FFAs) are important mediators of obesity-related inflammation.

pmc-11539714.title: The SH3-binding domain of chorismate mutase protein of Mycobacterium tuberculosis contributes to mycobacterial virulence
pmc-11539714.creator: Ravi Pal, Vandana Maurya, Supriya Borah, Sangita Mukhopadhyay
pmc-11539714.description: SummaryCrystal structure of the secretory chorismate mutase protein of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MtbCM) reveals presence of a proline rich region on its surface that serve as a recognition site for protein-protein interaction. This study shows that MtbCM upregulates IL-10 which favors M. tuberculosis by affecting PKCε-MKP-1-p38 MAPK signaling.

pmc-11577028.title: Vibrational noise disrupts Nezara viridula communication, irrespective of spectral overlap
pmc-11577028.creator: Rok Janža, Nataša Stritih-Peljhan, Aleš Škorjanc, Jernej Polajnar, Meta Virant-Doberlet
pmc-11577028.description: Insects rely on substrate vibrations in numerous intra- and interspecific interactions. Yet, our knowledge of noise impact in this modality lags behind that in audition, limiting our understanding of how anthropogenic noise affects insect communities. Auditory research has linked impaired signal perception in noise (i.e., masking) to spectral overlap.

pmc-12506553.title: The clinical utility and cost-effectiveness of routine vitamin B12 screening in adult psychiatric patients
pmc-12506553.creator: Tracy A. Hollander, Vidette M. Juby
pmc-12506553.description: BackgroundDiagnosing and treating vitamin B12 deficiency in psychiatric populations is important, but the justification for routine screening in patients without risk factors or physical findings remains uncertain, especially in resource-limited settings.AimThis study aimed to assess the clinical utility and cost-effectiveness of routine vitamin B12 screening in adult psychiatric inpatients.

pmc-12758101.title: Reinforcement Learning and Decision Making in Depression in Adolescents and Young Adults: Insights from a New Model of the Probabilistic Reward Task
pmc-12758101.creator: Ziwei Cheng, Amelia D Moser, Jenna Jones, Christopher D Schneck, David J Miklowitz, Daniel G Dillon, Roselinde H Kaiser
pmc-12758101.description: Depression is a prevalent psychiatric condition that commonly emerges in adolescence and young adulthood and is associated with reward processing abnormalities. The Probabilistic Reward Task (PRT) is widely used to investigate the impact of depression on reward processing, but prior studies have not comprehensively addressed the reinforcement learning and decision-making mechanisms involved in the task.

pmc-12778723.title: Post‐Market Registry of Stroke Patients Treated With Medtronic Neurothrombectomy Devices in Southeast Asia: PROSPR‐SEA
pmc-12778723.creator: Huy Thang Nguyen, Mai Duy Ton, Dang Luu Vu, Anchalee Churojana, Yongchai Nilanont, Sirintara (Pongpech) Singhara Na Ayudya, Deidre Anne De Silva, Winston Lim Eng Hoe, Truong Le Van, Minh Thong Pham, Thanaboon Worakijthamrongchai, Quoc Tuan Tran, Raymond Chee Seong Seet, Wickly Lee
pmc-12778723.description: BackgroundSoutheast Asia accounts for approximately 10% of stroke‐related mortalities worldwide, yet there are limited data regarding mechanical thrombectomy (MT) outcomes in this region. PROSPR‐SEA (Post‐Market Registry of Stroke Patients Treated With Medtronic Neurothrombectomy Devices to Collect Real‐World Data in Southeast Asia) assessed post‐market clinical outcomes of MT using the Solitaire Revascularization Device in southeast Asia.

pmc-12820338.title: Evolution of chromosomes and nuclear architectures of amniotes
pmc-12820338.creator: Jing Liu, Qi Zhou
pmc-12820338.description: Chromosomes of mammals and reptiles have diverged extensively in sequence and three-dimensional (3D) nuclear organization since their last common amniote ancestor. The fine-scale evolutionary patterns and mechanisms underlying this divergence and the relationship between chromosome rearrangements and 3D genome architecture remain unclear.

pmc-12966379.title: Analysis of different methods to calculate tertiary regulation reserves for renewable energy in Japan
pmc-12966379.creator: Joao G S Fonseca, Tatsuma Hori, Kazuhiko Ogimoto
pmc-12966379.description: Regulation reserves designed to compensate for renewable energy power generation unexpected shortfalls are being implemented around the world. In Japan, since 2021, the balancing market has a specific type of tertiary power regulation reserve to mitigate the effects of day-ahead forecasting errors of renewable energy systems.

pmc-13422184.title: Bacillus Calmette-Guérin as adjuvant platform enhances immunogenicity of conserved epitopes from structural proteins of SARS-CoV-2
pmc-13422184.creator: Ana de Souza Santos, Leonardo Pereira de Araújo, Diego Jose Belato Orts, Hernan Hermes Monteiro da Costa, Kely Catarine Matteucci, Evandro Neves Silva, Karen Cristina Oliveira, Giovane Galdino, Carlos Roberto Prudencio, Patrícia Paiva Corsetti, Leonardo Augusto de Almeida
pmc-13422184.description: The development of effective and broadly protective vaccines against SARS-CoV-2 remains a global priority. Conserved epitopes from viral structural proteins (E, M, N, and S) represent promising targets less affected by emerging mutations, while Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) offers unique adjuvant and delivery properties.
